answer: An operator books one numbered transit pier beneath a mapped zenith shaft. Only that holder may clamp a uniquely serialled glass plate to the shaft's guiding trellis and, at the catalogued comet culmination, open the shutter until the official sidereal clock stamps a numbered trail card. Graders match plate serial, shutter log, pier stamp, and clock hash. A shared pier, a reused plate, or an off-culmination exposure is forfeited as one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive piers, N unique plates, and N live culminations no single observer can cover in the same hour.
